title: Areas Associated with Cities
summary: Free-floating headings [city] Metropolitan Area, [city] Suburban Area and [city] Region are formed by inserting the phrase between the established city name and its qualifier (qualifier = jurisdiction of the city proper only); New York and Washington forms are unqualified. Two cities are never hyphenated together. City-only subdivisions are not used under these headings. As $z they are subdivided through the jurisdiction of the city proper, except New York, Washington, and Jerusalem metropolitan areas, which are used directly.
validation_rules: Form `[city] Metropolitan Area` by inserting `Metropolitan Area` between the established city name and its geographic qualifier: `Pensacola (Fla.)` → `Pensacola Metropolitan Area (Fla.)`. (H 790 sec. 1.a)
If the city name has no qualifier, append the phrase: `Jerusalem` → `Jerusalem Metropolitan Area`. (H 790 sec. 1.a)
Exception: `New York Metropolitan Area` and `Washington Metropolitan Area` have no geographic qualifiers even though the city names are qualified. (H 790 sec. 1.a)

If the metropolitan area spans two or more jurisdictions, qualify only by the jurisdiction of the city proper: `Binghamton Metropolitan Area (N.Y.)`, not `Binghamton Metropolitan Area (N.Y. and Pa.)`. (H 790 sec. 1.a)

Do not hyphenate two city names into one metropolitan area heading: use `Fort Worth Metropolitan Area (Tex.)` and `Dallas Metropolitan Area (Tex.)`, not `Dallas-Fort Worth Metropolitan Area (Tex.)`. (H 790 sec. 1.b)
Metropolitan area headings are used only for officially designated metropolitan areas; otherwise use the city region heading. (H 790 sec. 1.c)
Under metropolitan area headings use topical subdivisions appropriate to regions, countries, etc. (H 1140); do not use subdivisions used only under names of cities. (H 790 sec. 1.d)

As geographic subdivisions, metropolitan areas are subdivided through the jurisdiction in which the city proper is located, even if the area spans more than one country or first order division of Canada, Great Britain, or the United States: `Minorities--Missouri--Saint Louis Metropolitan Area`; qualifiers are deleted/retained per H 830. (H 790 sec. 1.e)

Exception: the New York, Washington, and Jerusalem metropolitan areas are used directly after topics: `Minorities--New York Metropolitan Area`; `Minorities--Washington Metropolitan Area`; `Minorities--Jerusalem Metropolitan Area`. (H 790 sec. 1.e)
`--Suburbs and environs` is discontinued (replaced in 1985 by the free-floating phrase `... Suburban Area`); do not use it. (H 790 sec. 2 Note)

`[city] Suburban Area` headings are constructed, assigned, and used as subdivisions exactly like metropolitan areas (insert before the qualifier; jurisdiction of the city proper; no hyphenated pairs); do not use city subdivisions under them. (H 790 sec. 2.a-c)

Form `[city] Region` by inserting `Region` between the established city name and its qualifier (`Pensacola Region (Fla.)`), or appending it to an unqualified city name (`Jerusalem Region`). (H 790 sec. 3.a)
Exception: `New York Region` and `Washington Region` have no geographic qualifiers. (H 790 sec. 3.a)
Do not construct a city region heading combining two city names with a hyphen. (H 790 sec. 3.b)
City regions are assigned like metropolitan areas; do not use subdivisions used only under names of cities under them. (H 790 sec. 3.c)

sections.heading: 1.a. Construction of headings
sections.text:
Construct free-floating headings for names of metropolitan areas by inserting the phrase Metropolitan Area between an established city name and its geographic qualifier. Example:

```
151 ## $a Pensacola (Fla.)
651 #0 $a Pensacola Metropolitan Area (Fla.)
```

If the city name has been established without a qualifier, add the phrase Metropolitan Area to the established form of the name. Example:

```
151 ## $a Jerusalem
651 #0 $a Jerusalem Metropolitan Area.
```

Exception: *New York Metropolitan Area* and *Washington Metropolitan Area* are established without geographic qualifiers even though the city names are qualified.

If a metropolitan area spreads across portions of two or more jurisdictions, qualify only by the name of the jurisdiction in which the city proper is located. Example:

```
151 ## $a Binghamton (N.Y.)
651 #0 $a Binghamton Metropolitan Area (N.Y.)
  [not 651 #0 $a Binghamton Metropolitan Area (N.Y. and Pa.)]
```

sections.heading: 1.b. Metropolitan areas that include two cities
sections.text:
Do not construct a heading for a single metropolitan area involving two cities by combining their names with a hyphen. Assign the metropolitan area of each city separately. Example:

```
651 #0 $a Fort Worth Metropolitan Area (Tex.)
651 #0 $a Dallas Metropolitan Area (Tex.)
  [not 651 #0 $a Dallas-Fort Worth Metropolitan Area (Tex.)]
```

sections.heading: 1.c. Metropolitan area headings vs. region headings
sections.text: Assign metropolitan areas as headings or subdivisions if there is evidence, either from the work being cataloged or from another acceptable source, that the proposed area has been officially designated a metropolitan area. Otherwise treat the area in question as a region related to the city.

sections.heading: 1.d. Topical subdivisions under metropolitan area headings
sections.text: Assign the name of the metropolitan area with appropriate topical subdivisions used under regions, countries, etc. (cf. H 1140). Do not assign subdivisions used only under names of cities.

sections.heading: 1.e. Metropolitan areas as geographic subdivisions
sections.text:
Assign metropolitan areas as geographic subdivisions through the jurisdiction in which the city proper is located, even if the metropolitan area spreads over more than a single country or first order political division in the case of Canada, Great Britain, and the United States. Follow the provisions of H 830 regarding the deletion or retention of information within parenthetical qualifiers. Example:

```
650 #0 $a Minorities $z Missouri $z Saint Louis Metropolitan Area.
```

Exception: The New York, Washington, and Jerusalem metropolitan areas are used directly after topics. Example:

```
650 #0 $a Minorities $z New York Metropolitan Area.
650 #0 $a Minorities $z Washington Metropolitan Area.
650 #0 $a Minorities $z Jerusalem Metropolitan Area.
```

sections.heading: 2. Suburban areas
sections.text: Note: The subdivision --Suburbs and environs was discontinued and replaced by the free-floating phrase ... Suburban Area in 1985. During the years 1979-1982 when neither the subdivision nor the phrase was in use, the corresponding city region or metropolitan area heading was used to designate the suburban area associated with a city.

sections.heading: 2.a. Construction of headings
sections.text: Construct headings for suburban areas by using the free-floating phrase ... Suburban Area, following the same provisions as for metropolitan areas, described above.

sections.heading: 2.b. Assignment of headings
sections.text: Assign these headings in the same manner prescribed for metropolitan areas. Do not use city subdivisions under these headings.

sections.heading: 2.c. Suburban areas as geographic subdivisions
sections.text: Assign suburban areas as geographic subdivisions according to the same principles described above for metropolitan areas.

sections.heading: 3.a. Construction of headings
sections.text:
Construct free-floating headings for city regions by inserting the word Region between an established city name and its geographic qualifier. Example:

```
151 ## $a Pensacola (Fla.)
651 #0 $a Pensacola Region (Fla.)
```

If the city name has been established without a qualifier, add the word Region to the established form of the name. Example:

```
151 ## $a Jerusalem
651 #0 $a Jerusalem Region.
```

Exception: *New York Region* and *Washington Region* are established without geographic qualifiers even though the city names are qualified.

sections.heading: 3.b. City regions that include two cities
sections.text: Do not construct a heading for a single region consisting of the names of two cities connected by a hyphen.

sections.heading: 3.c. Assignment of headings
sections.text: Assign city regions in the same manner prescribed for metropolitan areas above. Do not assign subdivisions used only under names of cities.
